defects.title: Item list endpoint returns every user's items to non-superusers (data leak)
defects.suspect_detail: read_items(), non-superuser else-branch: the `.where(Item.owner_id == current_user.id)` filter was removed from both the count statement and the item select statement
defects.root_cause: The diff deleted the owner_id filter in the non-superuser branch of GET /items/. That branch is now identical to the superuser branch, so any authenticated user gets all users' items and a global count.
defects.rationale: Both failures trace directly to the changed lines. TC-017 shows extra item IDs belonging to other users. TC-043 shows user B not getting the empty state because A's item is returned. Nothing suggests this is a deliberate rule change, since the page copy says 'Create and manage your items' and the single-item endpoints still enforce ownership with 403. This is a cross-tenant data exposure. The frontend is not at fault because it correctly renders whatever the API returns.
steps: Create user A and user B (non-superusers)
As A, POST /api/v1/items/ twice; as B, POST once
Alternatively, in the UI log in as B, who has no items, and open /items
defects.expected: A receives 200 with only A's 2 items and count=2. B sees the empty state 'You don't have any items yet'.
defects.actual: The response includes items owned by other users, and count covers all items in the table. B sees A's items instead of the empty state.

defects.title: Sign-up minimum password length raised from 8 to 10; boundary test still expects 8
defects.root_cause: UserRegister.password min_length was changed from 8 to 10, so POST /users/signup now returns 422 for an 8-character password. The test and plan still assume an 8-character minimum.
defects.rationale: Stricter password length looks like a deliberate security-policy change and not a defect, so the test is outdated. This is uncertain, because the change is only on UserRegister. UserCreate, UserUpdate, UpdatePassword and NewPassword still use min 8, and that inconsistency could be accidental. A human should confirm the intended policy. If 10 is intended, update TC-005 to use 10 and 128 as valid, 9 as invalid, and 129 as invalid, and decide whether the other schemas should follow. If it was unintended, revert the change.
steps: POST /api/v1/users/signup with a unique email and an 8-character password
defects.actual: 422 Unprocessable Content, because the password is shorter than the new 10-character minimum.
